questions.question: Complete the series: 4, 8, 16, 32, ?

Using a +2 letter shift cipher, "PILOT" becomes:

options.D: P,Q,R,T,S — determine best fit as A

questions.question: If "4" means "aircraft", "8" means "engine", "2" means "wing", what does "8 2" mean?
Find the missing term: BD, FH, JL, NP, ?

Choose the odd pair:

options.D: Turboprop–Air-breathing (rocket is the odd one, answer C)

questions.question: If East becomes South (90° clockwise rotation), then North becomes:
In a code, LAPTOP is written as MBQUPQ (+1 shift). How is DESKTOP written?
Statement: All metals are conductors. Copper is a metal. Conclusion: Copper is a conductor.
The momentum equation in fluid dynamics is derived from:

options.A: Newton's second law applied to a fluid control volume

questions.question: For a cambered airfoil, the moment coefficient about the aerodynamic center is typically:

options.B: A small negative constant, independent of angle of attack
options.C: Always positive and varying with CL

questions.question: The subsonic flow regime is generally considered to be Mach numbers:
Total drag on a subsonic aircraft is the sum of:
For minimum induced drag at a given lift, the ideal spanwise lift distribution is:

options.D: Uniform chord distribution regardless of lift

questions.question: A turbulent boundary layer, compared to laminar, is generally:

options.A: More resistant to flow separation but has higher skin friction

questions.question: In NACA airfoil "0012", the "00" indicates:
Reynolds number physically represents:

options.A: Ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces in a flow
options.D: Ratio of density to viscosity only

questions.question: Wave drag due to shock formation becomes significant starting at approximately which Mach number for typical airfoils?

options.B: The critical Mach number (often 0.7-0.85 depending on airfoil)

questions.question: The aerodynamic center for thin airfoil theory (incompressible, subsonic) lies at:
Increasing wing loading (weight/wing area) generally:

options.C: Has no effect on stall speed

questions.question: Fowler flaps increase CLmax primarily by:
The Prandtl-Glauert compressibility correction becomes increasingly important as Mach number approaches:
Across a normal shock wave, static pressure, temperature, and density all:

options.B: Increase, while Mach number decreases from supersonic to subsonic

questions.question: The lift-curve slope for a finite wing is generally ___ than the 2D (infinite span) value.

options.B: Lower (due to induced effects reducing effective angle of attack)

questions.question: Ground effect is most pronounced when the aircraft's height above ground is:

options.B: Comparable to or less than the wingspan (close to ground)

questions.question: For M = 1.5, the Mach angle is approximately:
Adverse yaw can be reduced/countered using:

options.A: Differential ailerons and/or coordinated rudder input

questions.question: Increasing aspect ratio for the same wing area generally:

options.B: Reduces induced drag but may increase structural weight

questions.question: Downwash angle behind a finite wing is directly related to:

options.A: Lift coefficient and aspect ratio (higher CL, lower AR → more downwash)

questions.question: The Kutta condition is applied at:

options.A: The leading edge of an airfoil
options.B: The sharp trailing edge of an airfoil

questions.question: Winglets function by:

options.A: Reducing the strength of wingtip vortices, effectively increasing efficiency
options.C: Adding weight with no aerodynamic benefit

questions.question: In a supersonic expansion around a convex corner, the flow:
Transonic wave drag is minimized in "coke-bottle" shaped fuselages due to application of:
Dynamic pressure q = ½ρV² is used directly in calculating:

options.A: Aerodynamic forces (lift, drag) via nondimensional coefficients

questions.question: In semi-monocoque construction, bending loads in the fuselage are shared between:
In an open thin-walled section under torsion, maximum shear stress occurs:

options.B: At the point of maximum thickness (for a given shape) generally near the outer fiber

questions.question: For a closed thin-walled section, the Bredt-Batho shear flow formula is q = T/(2A), where A represents:

options.B: Enclosed area within the median line of the section

questions.question: The primary structural role of a wing spar is to carry:

options.B: Bending moment and shear force due to lift distribution
options.D: Only aerodynamic pressure on the skin

questions.question: Fatigue cracks most commonly initiate at:

options.A: Regions of uniform stress with no discontinuities
options.B: Stress concentration features like rivet holes, notches, and fillets
options.C: The exact center of a solid bar
options.D: Locations under pure hydrostatic pressure only

questions.question: In the V-n diagram, the "n" axis represents:
Euler's buckling formula shows critical load is:

options.B: Inversely proportional to the square of the effective length

questions.question: Compared to aluminium, CFRP composites generally offer:

options.B: Higher stiffness/strength-to-weight ratio and better fatigue life

questions.question: The damage tolerance philosophy in aircraft design assumes:

options.A: No flaws can ever exist in a structure
options.B: Flaws may be present and structures must resist failure between scheduled inspections
options.C: Only static loads need be considered

questions.question: Longerons and stringers in a fuselage primarily resist:

options.B: Axial/bending stresses along the fuselage length

questions.question: A common ultimate load safety factor applied over limit load in aircraft structural design is:
The Von Mises criterion predicts yielding in ductile materials based on:

options.B: Distortion energy (equivalent stress) under combined loading

questions.question: Riveted lap joints are primarily designed to resist:
Titanium's key advantage over aluminium for high-temperature aerospace applications is:

options.B: Better retention of strength at elevated temperatures and good corrosion resistance

questions.question: A cylindrical pressurized fuselage under internal pressure p, radius r, thickness t has hoop stress approximately:
In monocoque construction, the outer skin:

options.B: Is the primary load-carrying member (no internal frame needed for primary loads)
options.C: Only provides aerodynamic shape with all load carried internally
options.D: Is always thicker than semi-monocoque skins

questions.question: Wing ribs primarily serve to:

options.A: Carry the full spanwise bending moment
options.B: Maintain the airfoil cross-sectional shape and distribute local loads to spars/skin
options.D: Provide the primary torsional stiffness of the fuselage

questions.question: The relationship σ = Eε (within elastic limit) defines:
Fatigue crack growth is commonly modeled using Paris' Law relating:

options.A: da/dN to ΔK (stress intensity factor range)

questions.question: Honeycomb sandwich panels achieve high bending stiffness at low weight primarily because:

options.A: The core material is very dense
options.B: Separating stiff face-sheets by a lightweight core increases the effective second moment of area
options.D: They eliminate the need for face-sheets

questions.question: Yield strength is the stress at which:
Aeroelasticity studies the interaction of:

options.A: Aerodynamic forces, elastic (structural) forces, and inertial forces

questions.question: Flutter involves:

options.B: A self-excited, potentially divergent oscillation from coupled bending-torsion modes interacting with airflow
options.D: Only tire vibration on the runway

questions.question: Creep in materials refers to:

options.B: Slow, time-dependent plastic deformation under sustained stress, worsened at elevated temperature
options.C: Deformation that fully reverses on unloading
options.D: A phenomenon only in brittle ceramics

questions.question: Compression-loaded stiffened panels commonly fail by:

options.B: Local skin buckling between stringers or overall panel buckling

questions.question: The gas turbine engine's ideal cycle (Brayton cycle) consists of which four processes?

options.A: Isothermal compression, isobaric heat addition, isothermal expansion, isobaric heat rejection
options.B: Isentropic compression, isobaric heat addition, isentropic expansion, isobaric heat rejection

questions.question: High bypass turbofans achieve better fuel economy at subsonic cruise mainly by:

options.A: Increasing exhaust velocity far above flight speed
options.B: Moving a larger mass of air at a lower velocity increment (higher propulsive efficiency)

questions.question: Bypass ratio (BPR) is mathematically:
In turbofan/turbojet engines, net thrust arises from:

options.A: The net rate of change of momentum of the air/gas passing through the engine (plus pressure term)
options.B: Only static pressure differences with zero velocity change

questions.question: The compressor's job in the Brayton cycle is analogous to which process?

options.B: Isentropic compression, raising pressure and temperature of intake air

questions.question: Axial-flow compressors are favored in high-thrust jet engines mainly because of their:

options.A: Larger diameter for the same flow
options.B: Smaller frontal area and higher efficiency at large mass flows compared to centrifugal types
options.C: Lower pressure ratio per stage always being preferred

questions.question: The turbine stage extracts energy from combustion gases primarily to:

options.B: Drive the compressor (and fan, in turbofans)

questions.question: Turboprops achieve high efficiency at lower speeds mainly because:

options.A: The propeller efficiently accelerates a large mass of air at low velocity increment
options.B: They produce no thrust at low speed
options.C: They operate best at supersonic Mach numbers
options.D: They lack a gas generator core

questions.question: SFC (specific fuel consumption) for a jet engine is typically expressed in units of:

options.A: kg of fuel per hour per kg (or N) of thrust

questions.question: A convergent-only nozzle can accelerate exhaust flow up to:

options.B: Sonic velocity (Mach 1) at the throat, no further acceleration without divergent section

questions.question: Afterburning is typically used for:

options.B: Short bursts of additional thrust (e.g., takeoff, combat maneuvers) at the cost of very high fuel consumption

questions.question: Combustion chamber design must balance:

options.A: High pressure loss with incomplete combustion
options.B: Complete, stable combustion against acceptable total pressure loss and a suitable temperature profile for the turbine
options.C: Zero residence time with complete combustion

questions.question: Choked flow at a converging nozzle throat means:

options.A: Flow cannot be further accelerated at the throat regardless of further pressure ratio increase (Mach 1 fixed at throat)

questions.question: Turboshaft engines are the standard choice for:

options.B: Helicopters (driving the main rotor via a gearbox)

questions.question: Overall propulsive system efficiency is the product of:

options.A: Thermal efficiency (cycle) and propulsive efficiency (momentum transfer)
options.C: Aerodynamic efficiency of the airframe alone

questions.question: Ram compression at the intake becomes significant primarily at:

options.B: Higher flight Mach numbers, where decelerating the incoming air raises static pressure

questions.question: Nickel-based superalloys are chosen for turbine blades mainly due to:

options.B: Excellent high-temperature strength and creep resistance

questions.question: The diffuser section of an engine intake:

options.A: Increases flow velocity and decreases pressure
options.B: Decreases flow velocity and increases static pressure ahead of the compressor

questions.question: A key distinguishing feature of rocket propulsion versus air-breathing propulsion is:

options.B: Rockets carry their own oxidizer, enabling thrust generation even in vacuum

questions.question: Neglecting pressure thrust, net thrust is approximately:

options.D: F = constant regardless of exit velocity

questions.question: Specific impulse (Isp) essentially measures:

options.B: How efficiently a propulsion system converts propellant into thrust (impulse per unit weight of propellant)

questions.question: Compressor stall/surge is a flow instability that can be triggered by:

options.B: High angle of attack on compressor blades due to off-design operation, distorted inflow, or rapid throttle changes

questions.question: Propulsive efficiency approaches its theoretical maximum when:

options.A: Exhaust velocity is very high relative to flight velocity
options.B: Exhaust velocity approaches flight velocity (minimal excess kinetic energy left in the wake)

questions.question: Modern turbofan engine development trends (higher BPR, higher OPR) primarily aim to:

options.B: Reduce specific fuel consumption and noise while maintaining thrust requirements
options.C: Eliminate the need for a fan
options.D: Increase engine weight without efficiency gain

questions.question: Reheat between turbine stages and intercooling between compressor stages in a gas turbine cycle:

options.B: Can increase specific work output and/or thermal efficiency depending on cycle design

questions.question: An altimeter's operation is fundamentally based on:

options.A: Comparing static air pressure to a calibrated reference (standard atmosphere)

questions.question: The airspeed indicator computes indicated airspeed using:

options.B: The difference between total (pitot) pressure and static pressure (dynamic pressure)

questions.question: The attitude indicator (artificial horizon) relies on which gyroscopic property?

options.B: Rigidity in space, maintaining a fixed reference plane
options.C: Gimbal lock as a design feature

questions.question: An Inertial Navigation System accumulates position error over time mainly due to:

options.B: Integration drift from accelerometer/gyroscope biases over time

questions.question: Ailerons, elevator, and rudder are collectively referred to as:
Hydraulic actuators are preferred for large flight control surfaces because they provide:

options.A: Very low force output requiring manual assistance always
options.B: High force output in a compact, lightweight package

questions.question: In fly-by-wire aircraft, pilot control inputs are:

options.A: Sent directly via cables to control surfaces
options.B: Converted to electronic signals, processed by flight control computers, then sent to actuators
options.D: Only used for autopilot, not manual flight

questions.question: The Environmental Control System typically uses engine bleed air (or electric compressors in some designs) for:
VOR ground stations transmit signals that allow aircraft to determine:

options.B: Their bearing (radial) relative to the station

questions.question: Modern autopilot systems can typically manage:

options.B: Heading, altitude, airspeed, and often full approach/landing modes

questions.question: Electrically actuated landing gear systems use:

options.A: Only manual hand cranks in all aircraft
options.B: Electric motors/actuators, sometimes with hydraulic backup
options.C: Only pneumatic bottles with no electric involvement
options.D: Gravity extension exclusively in all designs

questions.question: A radar altimeter is especially useful during:

options.B: Approach and landing, providing accurate height above terrain

questions.question: Angle of Attack information is critical for:

options.B: Stall warning systems and flight control law computations

questions.question: Fuel management systems must handle:

options.A: Constant fuel center of gravity regardless of burn
options.B: Fuel transfer/balancing across tanks as fuel is consumed, maintaining CG within limits

questions.question: Flight Data Recorders are built to withstand:

options.A: Normal handling only, with no crash requirements
options.B: Severe impact, fire, and pressure conditions to survive accidents for investigation

questions.question: Weather radar returns are primarily used to identify:

options.A: Areas of precipitation and associated turbulence to aid route deviation

questions.question: The Air Data Computer combines pitot-static and temperature data to compute:

options.B: Airspeed, altitude, vertical speed, and Mach number

questions.question: TCAS resolution advisories provide pilots with:

options.A: Only a warning tone with no guidance
options.B: Specific climb/descend guidance to avoid a conflicting aircraft

questions.question: Aircraft AC electrical power is generated in flight typically by:

options.B: Battery power throughout the entire flight only
options.D: Fuel cells exclusively on all aircraft

questions.question: Spoilers are deployed to:

options.B: Reduce lift and add drag, useful during descent and after landing to aid braking

questions.question: A Ram Air Turbine deploys during emergencies to:

options.A: Provide backup electrical/hydraulic power using airflow-driven turbine

questions.question: ILS glideslope and localizer signals together provide:

options.B: Vertical (glideslope) and lateral (localizer) guidance for precision approach

questions.question: The APU allows an aircraft to have power for systems:

options.A: Only in flight, never on ground
options.B: On the ground without main engines running, and as a backup source in flight

questions.question: Standard aviation radio communication bands used between ATC and aircraft include:
Trim systems reduce pilot workload by:

options.B: Offsetting the aerodynamic force on a control surface so less manual force is needed to hold a setting
